examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}{二十歳|はたち}になります。
{二十歳|はたち}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}
{二十歳|はたち}から{選挙権|せんきょけん}がある。
examples.english: You have voting rights from age twenty.

examples.japanese: {二十歳|はたち}になったら、お{酒|さけ}が{飲|の}めるようになる。
examples.english: When you turn twenty, you can legally drink alcohol.

examples.japanese: {二十歳|はたち}のとき{成人式|せいじんしき}に{出|で}て、{友達|ともだち}とたくさん{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}った。
examples.english: At age twenty, I attended the coming-of-age ceremony and took lots of photos with friends.

notes:
{二十歳|はたち} is a special native Japanese reading for 'twenty years old.' It is an irregular reading — the regular Sino-Japanese form would be {二十|にじゅう}{歳|さい}.

SPECIAL AGE READINGS:
Japanese has very few special age words. {二十歳|はたち} is the most common. The regular counter pattern ～{歳|さい} is used for all other ages.

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
- Traditional age of adulthood in Japan
- {成人式|せいじんしき} (Coming of Age ceremony) is held for those turning 20
- Note: The legal adult age changed to 18 in April 2022, but {成人式|せいじんしき} is often still celebrated at 20

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {二十歳|はたち}になる: to turn twenty
- {二十歳|はたち}の{記念|きねん}: twentieth birthday commemoration
